{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_a66c74fa1d4a4f078f32f212","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error\n2\t\n3\tIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\n4\tLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n5\t\n6\t## Why\n7\t\n8\tThe orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n9\t\n10\t`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads \"no errors\" while the caller sees rejections.\n11\t\n12\tRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n13\t\n14\t## What to do\n15\t\n16\tCall `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.\n17\t\n18\t## Acceptance criteria\n19\t\n20\t- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged\n21\t- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`\n22\t- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n23\t- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n24\t- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n25\t\n26\t## Tech notes\n27\t\n28\tKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n29\t\n30\tOut of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n31\t\n32\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"36d2b93c-dafb-43c3-b3b8-4c273769c1ab","uuid":"bdf6930c-3ba1-4412-aa5e-0bc938f74bd2","timestamp":"2026-11-06T06:54:48.575Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/c1df428c256a/workspace/ticket.md","content":"# Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error\n\nIssue: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\nLabels: priority:medium, type:bug, size:S, area:api\n\n## Why\n\nThe orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a value from a library that rejects with its own shape — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n\n`onError` is the seam a deployer uses to count failures, page someone, or write an incident record. A gate that silently drops a class of failures makes it a liar in exactly the cases nobody tested for, and the deployer's dashboard reads \"no errors\" while the caller sees rejections.\n\nRecorded as measured behaviour in `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` by HALEngine#83, which scoped itself to specifying the seam rather than changing it, and raised again by the reviewer on that PR. The spec notes this property is owned by no issue in the epic; this is that issue.\n\n## What to do\n\nCall `onError` for every rejection. Whatever is not already an `Error` gets wrapped in one, preserving the original as the `cause`, so a hook typed against `Error` keeps compiling and a hook that wants the raw value can still reach it. The re-thrown value at the caller boundary stays exactly what it is today, so nothing downstream changes shape.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] A provider rejecting with a string calls `onError` once, with an `Error` whose `cause` is that string, and the caller still receives the original rejection unchanged\n- [ ] The same holds for a rejection with a plain object and with `undefined`\n- [ ] A rejection that is already an `Error` reaches `onError` as the same instance, not a wrapper, pinned by the existing tests remaining unedited\n- [ ] `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md` replaces its recorded-flaw line with the new guarantee, and the CHANGELOG says what changes for an existing consumer\n- [ ] `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run eslint` (`--max-warnings 0`) and `npm run prettier:check` pass\n\n## Tech notes\n\nKey files: `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` (the `catch` and its `instanceof Error` gate), `specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md`.\n\nOut of scope: `beforeSession` escaping the `try` (its own issue) and usage accounting across tool rounds (HALEngine#93).\n\n","numLines":32,"startLine":1,"totalLines":32}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_a66c74fa1d4a4f078f32f212","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_2c1ede699a2b4daa9aeddab2","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Definition of Done\n2\t\n3\t> The orchestrator's `catch` gates `onError` on `error instanceof Error`. A rejection that is not an `Error` — a thrown string, a plain object, a response body rejected directly by an HTTP client — bypasses `onError` entirely while still propagating to the caller.\n4\t\n5\t**Strategy: `direct`** — the seam already exists. `createChatOrchestrator` returns an orchestrator whose `processMessage` and `processMessageStream` invoke the installed `OrchestratorHooks`. A test can drive `processMessage` with a provider that throws a string or a plain object and observe that `onError` is bypassed today because of the `error instanceof Error` gate in the `catch` block.\n6\t\n7\t## Done when these pass\n8\t\n9\t- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing** — when a turn rejects with a string (`'string boom'`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance whose `message` is `'string boom'`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. Fails today because `onError` is skipped (`callOrder` is `['afterSession']` and `isError` is `false`).\n10\t      `src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts`\n11\t\n12\t- [ ] **calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object** — when a turn rejects with a plain object (`{code: 503, detail: 'upstream down'}`), `onError` is called once with an `Error` instance carrying a non-empty `message`, `afterSession` runs after `onError`, and the rejection still propagates to the caller. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_4c130be493e747a89b2e5052","type":"tool_result","content":"commit 64143f70d171548198336e81e6c5a2cee685d35f\nAuthor: loop-bench <loop-bench@localhost>\nDate:   Tue Oct 20 11:31:37 2026 +0200\n\n    test(orchestrator): pin onError on non-Error rejection\n\n .lore/dod.md                                       | 25 +++++++\n specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md              |  7 +-\n .../onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts             | 81 ++++++++++++++++++++++\n 3 files changed, 107 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)\n\ncommit 2ce51623df00d6437619309ef215f357ddbfea1b\nAuthor: loop-bench <loop-bench@localhost>\nDate:   Fri Nov 6 07:51:32 2026 +0100\n\n    fix(orchestrator): report non-Error rejections\n    \n    Every rejection inside a turn now reaches onError: a non-Error value is\n    wrapped with a readable message and the original as cause, while the\n    caller still receives the original rejection unchanged.\n    \n    Refs: re-cinq/HALEngine#95\n    Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>\n\n .lore/dod.md                                   |  8 +++++---\n CHANGELOG.md                                   |  1 +\n specs/hal-engine-architecture/spec.md          | 26 +++++++++++++-------------\n specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md          |  4 ++--\n specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md |  2 +-\n src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts     | 19 ++++++++++++++++++-\n src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts          | 11 ++++++++---\n 7 files changed, 48 insertions(+), 23 deletions(-)\n----\n9:## [Unreleased]\n10-\n11-### Added\n12-\n13-- `SessionStore` gains an optional `save(session)` member: the write signal a durable store needs. The engine calls it once per processed user message, from the same `finally` path that runs `afterSession`, so it fires for a turn that ended in a provider error as well as one that succeeded — a store that only heard about successes would lose exactly the conversations a customer complains about. By the time it runs, the turn's entries are committed, so the assistant entry's `isStreaming` is already `false` — including when a provider threw mid-stream, where the engine now closes the open entry before saving, recording `truncated` on it, rather than persisting a half-streamed entry that looks finished. An `afterSession` hook that throws no longer costs the turn its write signal. What `save` throws or rejects with is caught and logged as one line carrying the session id, and the turn continues: the client still receives its full stream and `stream_end`, because a database outage is not a reason for the agent to stop answering. The member is typed `void | Promise<void>`, so a synchronous implementation and an `async` one both satisfy it. Additive: `InMemorySessionStore` does not implement `save` and is unchanged, and a store that omits it behaves exactly as before.\n14-- `SessionStore` gains an optional `evict(sessionId)` member, and `InMemorySessionStore` implements it. The engine calls it only for a session whose socket closed while `create` was still pending — one that no client ever received and that has no entries to keep. `InMemorySessionStore` now also takes `{maxAgeMs}` (default `28_800_000`, eight hours), exported as `InMemorySessionStoreOptions`. Expired sessions are evicted when read and swept at the head of `create`, which stops at the first live session, so the bound costs nothing on a busy store. There is no timer: a library-owned interval would keep your process alive.\n15-- **`MongoSessionStore`**, a durable session store, exported as `MongoSessionStore` and `createMongoSessionStore`. It takes a collection, a client with a database name, or a connection URL — nothing in the package reads the environment or assumes a host. The collection is the truth and the in-process cache is an optimisation: a session written by `save` is readable by a second store on the same collection. `delete` removes the document — it is the consumer's erasure primitive and the engine never calls it — as do `eraseConversation`, `eraseOlderThan(cutoff)` and `eraseAll`, while `clear` alone touches only the cache; `docs/session-stores.md` opens with the table that says which is which, because the previous documentation would have led you to believe `delete` erased. Documents carry `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, so a retention period is expressible without per-entry timestamps. **No credential is ever written**: `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` and `host` are stripped at any depth, not just the top level, and the same `stripCredentialKeys` is exported for stores you write yourself. `mongodb` is an optional peer dependency loaded only when the store actually connects, so a consumer who installs no optional peer can still import the package root and use the in-memory store. **Migration note**: `delete` and `evict` both erase on this store, so the one-line `onDisconnect: sessionId => store.delete(sessionId)` that restores the pre-0.4 close behaviour destroys the conversation on every socket close — point `onDisconnect` at neither. Nothing needs reclaiming by hand: the in-process cache is bounded by `maxAgeMs` (eight hours by default) and drops stale entries without touching a document. This does **not** deliver conversation resume, and it does not make the engine safe to run as more than one instance against one conversation.\n16-- `withRetry(provider, policy)` decorator wraps any `AIProvider` with per-attempt retry and timeout logic. Pass it a `RetryPolicy` — all fields optional — to absorb transient provider failures before they reach the caller. Defaults: `maxAttempts: 3`, `baseDelayMs: 500`, `maxDelayMs: 5000`, `firstChunkTimeoutMs: 30000`, `idleChunkTimeoutMs: 30000`. A hung request (first chunk never arrives) is abandoned and retried; a stalled stream (idle after the first chunk) surfaces as an `AIError` with code `TIMEOUT` and is not retried, because chunks already streamed cannot be un-sent. Backoff is exponential with full jitter. Both `withRetry` and `RetryPolicy` are exported from the package root.\n17-- `HalEngineConfig` gains an optional `resilience?: RetryPolicy` field. When present, `createHalEngine` wraps the provider with `withRetry` between `createProvider` and `createChatOrchestrator`; when absent, behaviour is unchanged. This is a strictly additive change — no existing call to `createHalEngine` is affected, so the version bump is MINOR.\n18-\n19-### Changed\n20-\n21-- Every `SessionStore` member is now `Awaitable<T>` (`T | Promise<T>`) rather than a bare `T`, so a store backed by a database is expressible for the first time. `Awaitable` is exported from the package root. **A synchronous implementation needs no change** — `T` is assignable to `T | Promise<T>` in a return position — and `InMemorySessionStore` is unedited. The WebSocket connection handler now awaits `create` and the release that follows a close: it pauses the socket across the await so a frame sent before `connected` arrives is buffered rather than dropped, attaches its `close` listener before the await so a socket that closes mid-create leaves no session behind, and catches a rejection from either call so one store failure closes one socket instead of ending the process with an unhandled rejection. **Migration note**: the `connected` frame now arrives one tick later, after the awaited `create`, so a client that waits for it (as the protocol already requires) sees no difference; only code that assumed the frame was emitted synchronously with the upgrade does.\n--\n253:[Unreleased]: https://github.com/re-cinq/HALEngine/compare/v0.3.0...main\n254-[0.3.0]: https://github.com/re-cinq/HALEngine/releases/tag/v0.3.0\n255-[0.2.1]: An `afterSession` hook called under this condition can infer the session never advanced past `beforeSession`: no user-input hooks ran, no model response was generated, and no tool rounds were started — a cleanup hook that allocates in `beforeSession` and frees in `afterSession` will therefore always see the allocation and the release on the same error path ([validated by: runs onError then afterSession when it throws, and still rejects to the caller](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L116)).\n19:- Any rejection inside the turn calls `onError` with an `Error` — passed through when the thrown value is already an `Error`, or wrapped with a readable `message` and the original value as `cause` when it is not — and then runs `afterSession` while still propagating the rejection to the caller ([validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying the thrown string and runs afterSession while rethrowing](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L53), [validated by: calls onError with an Error carrying a readable message when the stream rejects with a plain object](../../src/orchestration/onErrorNonError.acceptance.test.ts#L64), [validated by: hands onError an Error whose cause is the thrown string while the caller still receives the string](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L311)).\n----\n# Lore test-command interface (lore_list_tests / lore_run_test).\n# Written for this repo's Jest suite rather than adapted from the Vitest\n# equivalent for a Vitest suite: the report shapes happen to match, but the\n# invocations do not.\n- id: hal-engine-jest\n  name: HAL Engine Jest suite\n  cwd: .\n  description: >-\n    The ts-jest unit suite over src/ and scripts/ (jest.config.js roots), run\n    on every pull request in .github/workflows/ci.yml as the \"Test\" step.\n    Selectors are \"<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>\" as emitted by the\n    list command. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_a5dfc67250144f63883603cd","type":"tool_result","content":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Emits the Lore test-command `list` shape: a single JSON array of\n// {id, name, file} objects, one per test, and nothing else on stdout.\n// Jest cannot resolve test names without executing them - there is no\n// dry-run - so the suite is run once with --json written to a temp file and\n// progress sent to stderr, keeping stdout pure.\n// The id is \"<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>\" - stable across runs,\n// and exactly what the run command's {selector} splits back apart.\nimport {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';\nimport {readFileSync, rmSync} from 'node:fs';\nimport {tmpdir} from 'node:os';\nimport {join, relative} from 'node:path';\nimport process from 'node:process';\n\nconst reportFile = join(tmpdir(), `hal-engine-jest-report-${process.pid}.json`);\n\ntry {\n  execFileSync('npx', ['jest', '--json', `--outputFile=${reportFile}`], {\n    cwd: process.cwd(),\n    stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'inherit'],\n    // The suite runs as ESM; jest needs the flag in every spawn, not just npm test.\n    env: {...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: `${process.env.NODE_OPTIONS ?? ''} --experimental-vm-modules`.trim()},\n  });\n} catch {\n  // A failing test still produces a full report, and listing must not depend\n  // on the suite being green. An unreadable report below is the real failure.\n}\n\nlet report;\n\ntry {\n  report = JSON.parse(readFileSync(reportFile, 'utf8'));\n} catch (error) {\n  process.stderr.write(`jest produced no readable report at ${reportFile}: ${error.message}\\n`);\n  process.exit(1);\n} finally {\n  rmSync(reportFile, {force: true});\n}\n\nconst tests = report.testResults.flatMap(suite => {\n  const file = relative(process.cwd(), suite.name);\n\n  return suite.assertionResults.map(assertion => ({\n    id: `${file}::${assertion.fullName}`,\n    name: assertion.fullName,\n    file,\n  }));\n});\n\nprocess.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(tests)}\\n`);","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"36d2b93c-dafb-43c3-b3b8-4c273769c1ab","uuid":"02b635fe-a9c1-4b5c-9656-ae6e7d1cb88b","timestamp":"2026-11-06T06:57:30.071Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"#!/usr/bin/env node\n// Emits the Lore test-command `list` shape: a single JSON array of\n// {id, name, file} objects, one per test, and nothing else on stdout.\n// Jest cannot resolve test names without executing them - there is no\n// dry-run - so the suite is run once with --json written to a temp file and\n// progress sent to stderr, keeping stdout pure.\n// The id is \"<repo-relative-file>::<full test name>\" - stable across runs,\n// and exactly what the run command's {selector} splits back apart.\nimport {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';\nimport {readFileSync, rmSync} from 'node:fs';\nimport {tmpdir} from 'node:os';\nimport {join, relative} from 'node:path';\nimport process from 'node:process';\n\nconst reportFile = join(tmpdir(), `hal-engine-jest-report-${process.pid}.json`);\n\ntry {\n  execFileSync('npx', ['jest', '--json', `--outputFile=${reportFile}`], {\n    cwd: process.cwd(),\n    stdio: ['ignore', 'ignore', 'inherit'],\n    // The suite runs as ESM; jest needs the flag in every spawn, not just npm test.\n    env: {...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: `${process.env.NODE_OPTIONS ?? ''} --experimental-vm-modules`.trim()},\n  });\n} catch {\n  // A failing test still produces a full report, and listing must not depend\n  // on the suite being green. An unreadable report below is the real failure.\n}\n\nlet report;\n\ntry {\n  report = JSON.parse(readFileSync(reportFile, 'utf8'));\n} catch (error) {\n  process.stderr.write(`jest produced no readable report at ${reportFile}: ${error.message}\\n`);\n  process.exit(1);\n} finally {\n  rmSync(reportFile, {force: true});\n}\n\nconst tests = report.testResults.flatMap(suite => {\n  const file = relative(process.cwd(), suite.name);\n\n  return suite.assertionResults.map(assertion => ({\n    id: `${file}::${assertion.fullName}`,\n    name: assertion.fullName,\n    file,\n  }));\n});\n\nprocess.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(tests)}\\n`);","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_a5dfc67250144f63883603cd","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_da7c92e786394f5aa4f1b067","type":"tool_result","content":"## Spec Test Links\n\nStatements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\nparenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\nstatement and a paragraph counts per sentence. Tests live beside their source\nin this repo, so the path points into `src/`:\n\n```markdown\n- All entries within a single assistant response are committed before the next\n  user message is processed\n  ([validated by: commits every entry before the next user message](../../src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts#L42)).\n```\n\nThe citation carries the test's **name** as well as its line. The name is what the\nauthor cited; the line is a derived pointer, and it goes stale on its own - adding\nan import above a suite moves every test below it, and the citation lands on a\ndifferent, still-valid declaration without anything noticing. `npm run spec:names`\nholds each citation to the test it names, and `npm run spec:names:fix` repoints the\nline from the name. The `#Lnn` stays because the lint rule and the coverage job\nboth index by it; a citation without one marks the whole file covered rather than\none test.\n\nA citation counts as coverage only where it is trailing, and a test link placed\nanywhere else in the statement is a misplaced citation rather than a weaker one.\nUpstream `check:spec-links` reports it and exits 1, and the coverage job that\nconsumes these specs records nothing for it - so a spec can read as fully cited while its coverage is\nzero. A mid-statement link to something that is not a test file - a script, a\ndoc, another spec - is ordinary prose, is never reported, and was never coverage\nto begin with. A misplaced citation is fixed by moving it to the end of its\nstatement, never by deleting it.\n\nIn a test file the `#Lnn` anchor must land on the `it(`, `test(` or `describe(`\ndeclaration itself - not a blank line, not one holding only closing punctuation,\nand not a line inside the test body. A citation onto an `expect` renders and\nresolves like any other, and proves nothing: no reader can turn that line back\ninto the name of a case. `scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` reports all four as\n`rotten` and exits 1 in both modes. A citation into a file that is not a test -\na workflow, a config, `package.json` - has no declaration to land on and is held\nonly to existing and carrying content.\n\nWhat no gate can catch is an anchor aimed at the wrong declaration: a real but\nunintended `it(` passes every check. The tell is that the test the statement\nmeant to cite goes on reading as uncited in the `require-spec-link` backlog.\n\nAnchors drift silently whenever a cited file gains or loses lines above them, so\nafter editing any cited file re-run `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs`\nrather than hand-correcting the numbers. That script cannot repair a spec absent\nfrom the base ref, since it has no baseline to translate from; on the branch that\nintroduces a spec, its anchors have to be corrected by hand.\n\nThe convention's tooling is wired up here: `npm run check:spec-links`, `npm run check:spec-status` and\n`node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main` all gate CI, and\n`re-lint/require-status-matches-coverage` derives each `Status` row from its\nspec's citations. `re-lint/require-spec-link` gates in `eslint.config.mjs`: every test cites a\nstatement, so an uncited new test fails the build. Its statement-side mirror,\n`require-statement-links`, runs at `warn` from `eslint.config.backlog.mjs` and\nreports without blocking - the severities the rule pair is designed for.","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"36d2b93c-dafb-43c3-b3b8-4c273769c1ab","uuid":"3df64c41-3319-4429-8da0-8a7ed0dbc66a","timestamp":"2026-11-06T06:57:46.223Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"## Spec Test Links\n\nStatements in `specs/*/spec.md` cite their validating test in a trailing\nparenthetical at the end of the statement, where a list item counts as one\nstatement and a paragraph counts per sentence.
